paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the relationship between 'Rank' and 'Errors (RTE)'. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” with a linear scale ranging from 4 to 256, incrementing by factors of 4; the tick labels are 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis is labeled “Errors (RTE)” with a linear scale ranging from 0.3 to 0.9, incrementing by 0.1; the tick labels are 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, and 0.9.  A single green line with circular markers represents the data. At a rank of 4, the value is approximately 0.3 with an error bar extending from approximately 0.25 to 0.35.  At a rank of 16, the value is approximately 0.35 with an error bar extending from approximately 0.3 to 0.4. At a rank of 64, the value is approximately 0.45 with an error bar extending from approximately 0.4 to 0.5, then it increases to approximately 0.65 at a rank of 256 with an error bar extending from approximately 0.6 to 0.7.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the relationship between rank and errors, represented with error bars. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” with a linear scale ranging from 4 to 256, with tick labels at intervals of 4, 16, 64, and 256, and no units specified. The y-axis is labeled “Errors (RTE)” with a linear scale ranging from 0.3 to 0.9, with tick labels at intervals of 0.3. A single black solid line is plotted, with green circular markers at each data point, and error bars indicating uncertainty. At a rank of 4, the line begins at approximately 0.32, and remains relatively level until a rank of 16 where it is about 0.33. Between a rank of 16 and 64, the line declines to approximately 0.47. From a rank of 64 to 256, the line increases to approximately 0.65.
